newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-VASCO FANS SHOUT "FIX" AFTER INJURY TIME WIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-VASCO FANS SHOUT "FIX" AFTER INJURY TIME WIN.

text.p: Vasco da Gama fans chanted "robbery" and "it's a fix" after their own team scored in the fourth and sixth minute of injury time to beat Volta Redonda 2-1 in a Rio de Janeiro championship match.

In yet another tumultuous game, referee Carlos Alberto Dutra was chased off the pitch by furious Volta Redonda players and officials. One unidentified man kicked the referee from behind just before he reached the dressing-room, causing him to fall over.
Volta Redonda, considered one of the competition's small teams, had taken a fifth-minute lead in the game at Vasco's ground on Wednesday night.

The fans' suspicions were aroused at the start of the second half, when Volta Redonda had Fabinho and Denilson sent off, apparently for arguing. Volta Redonda still managed to hold on for the rest of the second half, until Vasco midfielder Ramon equalised in the fourth minute of injury time.
The referee was immediately surrounded by protesting Volta Redonda players, causing the almost inevitable pitch invasion with police, reporters and hangers-on all rushing onto the field.
The referee told radio and television reporters on the pitch that he would add play two minutes once the game re-started and in the 96th minute of play, Ramon struck again.
Far from celebrating, Vasco's own fans protested with their chants at the end.
Referee Dutra refused to comment as he left the stadium.
The result left Volta Redonda bottom of the second stage, with three defeats in three games, while Vasco went level on points with Botafogo at the top.
The Rio championship began inauspiciously with Botafogo, Flamengo and Fluminense boycotting the opening weekend because they did not like the format and has been dogged by confusion ever since.

Several matches have been interrupted by brawls in which police, reporters, officials and hangers-on have invaded the field to join in. In one game, the coach of Itaperuna was so angry with the referee that he ran onto the pitch, ripped off his shirt and dropped his trousers to protest.
The Brazilian public was stunned when Flamengo's star striker Romario became involved in a fight with another player on the pitch but was let off by the Rio federation because of "lack of evidence."
Meanwhile, the format of the competition is so complicated that almost nobody fully understands it.
A newspaper last week asked 15 players the same four questions about the rules and said that none got all the answers right.
